identity.name: Zeta (Balšić lordship)
alt_names: Lordship of Zeta and the Coast

land.text: Zeta and the western lands of Emperor Urosh: the Balsic had been 'rulers of the state under Tsar Urosh' from 1360 and 'created a regional principality sometime after 1360'; after Marica 'Emperor Urosh died in 1371 and no one succeeded him'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's 1375 shape also holds Kosovo, which the pages give to Vuk Brankovic and the Lazarevic. The Serbian Empire dossier lists this row as successor for 'Zeta, Kosovo and the lords of the west'.

land.text: Zeta, which Balsa III 'passed' to his uncle Despot Stefan Lazarevic in 1421; 'after its incorporation into the Serbian Despotate in 1421, Zeta was organized as a single large Vlast'

successors.note: Balsa III died on 28 April 1421. The Serbian Despotate page's infobox lists 'Zeta under the Balsici' among the despotate's predecessors.

capitals.name: Scutari (Shkodër)
capitals.note: The Balšić noble family page: 'The administrative and political center of Balša's feudal entity between 1355 and 1396 was the city of Shkodër'. Đurađ II's edict was 'issued ... on 28 January 1386 in Scutari' (Đurađ II page); he handed Scutari to Venice in April 1396, so the seat moves in 1396. The Ottoman occupation of Scutari in 1393 is in the ledger and does not move the capital here.

capitals.name: Ulcinj
capitals.note: Đurađ II 'made Ulcinj his seat and the family seat' (undated), died there in April 1403 and ruled directly only 'Bar and Ulcinj' by 1396; the Venetians seized Ulcinj in 1405 (Balsa III page). Balsa III's seat 1405-1417 is not given on the pages.

capitals.name: Scutari (Shkodër)
capitals.note: 1418: Balsa III 'conquered Shkodër from the Venetians'.

rulers.name: Đurađ I Balšić
rulers.title: Lord of Zeta
rulers.note: The page: 'was the Lord of Zeta between 1362 and 13 January 1378' (infobox 'Reign: 1362–1378'); the dossier starts in 1371. 'recent studies now conclude that Đurađ died in 1379 rather than in 1378.' Balša I and Stracimir come before him and are only in the family tree of the Balšić page (undated).

rulers.name: Balša II Balšić
rulers.title: Lord of Zeta
rulers.note: 'The rule of Zeta was passed down to his younger brother, Balša II.' He was killed at Savra on 18 September 1385 (Battle of Savra and Đurađ II pages); the Savra page has him call himself 'Duke of Durrës' in a charter to Ragusa. The title is the researcher's wording; no page opened gives Balša II's title.

rulers.name: Đurađ II Balšić
rulers.title: Lord of Zeta and the Coast
rulers.note: 18 September 1385 (death of his uncle Balsa II at Savra) to April 1403; his predecessors Đurađ I and Balša II are the two entries above (Đurađ I page); Balša I and Stracimir are undated on the pages opened.

rulers.name: Balša III
rulers.title: Lord of Zeta
rulers.note: April 1403 to 28 April 1421; 'in 1421 ... he passed the rule of Zeta' to Stefan Lazarević.

correction.text: the 1375 outline for the first two years: Zeta with Shkodër and the Albanian coast, and the Kosovo land of Prizren ('took Prizren from Marko' in 1371) and Peć ('a year later')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the dossier starts in 1371 (Marica, the end of Urosh's rule; the Balšić page: 'Following the Battle of Maritsa and the collapse of Serbian central state authority they were able to establish their own independent state') but Cliopatria's first shape is 1375. The Đurađ I page dates Prizren to 1371 and Peć 'a year later' (1372), so the 1375 outline has Peć a year early. No page gives an area (the Balšić page has no infobox area).

union.text: the towns of Trebinje, Konavle and Dračevica (Herceg Novi), reaching 'north to the borders of Dubrovnik's territory'

correction.text: the 1375 outline plus the coast Đurađ I took from Altomanović and held 'briefly between 1373 and 1377': Trebinje, Konavle and Dračevica (Herceg Novi)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1373-1376: Cliopatria's 1375 outline holds no cell of Herceg Novi or Trebinje (gazetteer check: 0 cells for Herceg Novi), but the Đurađ I page has Đurađ gaining 'the towns of Trebinje, Konavle and Dračevica (Herceg Novi) from Altomanović' and the Balšić page quotes Fine that the lands reached the Dubrovnik border 'briefly between 1373 and 1377'. About 3,000 km2 added (30,350 km2 by cell count against 27,310 km2 for the outline alone, Trebinje being a large municipality); Tvrtko I annexed it in 1377 (ledger).

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1377 only: Zeta, the Skadar-Drivast-Lezhë coast and the Kosovo land (7,590 km2) after Tvrtko I annexed the Trebinje-Konavle-Dračevica coast 'in 1377' and before Vuk Branković took Prizren after the death of Đurađ I (1378)

keyframe_review.note: The shape as drawn (29,468 km2: Montenegro 9,870, Kosovo 7,590, Albania 5,570 km2, which together are 23,030 km2; the table assigns the other ~6,400 km2 to no country, probably Lake Skadar and Adriatic cells) is right for one year only. 1373-1376 are the new 1373 keyframe (outline plus the coast), 1378-1385 the new 1378 keyframe (Kosovo lost), 1386 on the new 1386 keyframe (the strip). No infobox area exists to compare with (Balšić page: none).

correction.text: the 1375 outline without Kosovo: 'Vuk Branković took Prizren and other land in Kosovo' at 'the end of the 1370s'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe closing the unexplained fall of the area: Cliopatria's 1375 outline (29,468 km2) keeps Kosovo to 1394, but the Balšić page says 'The Balšić holdings declined at the end of the 1370s' with Branković taking Prizren and other land in Kosovo, and the Đurađ I page has Branković seizing Prizren 'along with the rest of Đurađ's holdings in the region' after Đurađ I's death (13 January 1378; a later study says 1379). Kosovo out: about 19,730 km2 by cell count (27,310 km2 for the whole outline by the same count). Conflict: the Đurađ II page lists 'Vuk Branković took Peć and Prizren' among the secessions after Savra (1385-86) without a date; the dossier follows the two pages that date it to the late 1370s.

correction.text: the Zeta core: Scutari, Drivast, Ulcinj, Bar and the strip between Lake Skadar and the Adriatic ('a strip between Lake Skadar and the Adriatic')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the secessions that follow Savra (ledger 1386-1387: Lezhë and the Drin, the Jonima lands, Onogošt, Budva) 'Đurađ's demesne had diminished into a small strip of land between Lake Skadar and the Adriatic Sea'. Cliopatria's 1415 outline (6,578 km2) is the nearest drawn extent. The area falls from about 19,730 km2 (1378 keyframe) to about 6,580 km2: the ledger names Lezhë/Drin (~1,500 km2), the Jonima lands (~1,300), Nikšić (~1,800) and Budva (~250), which leaves ~8,000 km2 of the Zeta interior that no page assigns to a holder (the page has Đurađ in constant conflicts with Radič Crnojević in the Zeta plains under Lovćen). Kotor (March 1391 to the Crnojević of 1392, ledger) is a few cells and is not drawn. No infobox area exists to compare with.

correction.text: the Zeta core without Shkodër from April 1396: 'By 1396 he directly ruled only a small area west of the Bojana river, with Bar and Ulcinj as his only cities'

keyframe_review.note: 27,364 km2 for 1395-1401 is far too large: Đurađ II handed Scutari, Lake Skadar and Drivast to Venice in April 1396 and ruled 'only a small area west of the Bojana river'. 1395 itself still belongs to the 1386 keyframe; 1396-1401 to the new 1396 keyframe.

correction.text: Zeta west of the Bojana with Bar and Ulcinj, without Shkodër (handed to Venice in April 1396)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the April 1396 contract Venice holds Scutari, the lake and Drivast (Đurađ II page: 'handed over Scutari, the Skadar Lake with all its islands and Sveti Srđ to Venetian administration').

correction.text: the Zeta core without Shkodër, Venetian 1396-1418; Ulcinj, Bar and Budva lost in 1405

keyframe_review.note: 27,340 km2 for 1402-1414: Balsa III inherited Zeta in April 1403 (the page names Zeta, Shkodër, Ulcinj, Bar, Budva), lost Ulcinj, Bar and Budva to Venice in 1405 and retook Bar in 1412; Kosovo, Prizren and Pec were Brankovic's. The new 1396, 1405 and 1412 keyframes replace it.

correction.text: Zeta without Shkodër (Venetian since 1396) and without the coast Venice seized in 1405

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1405, Ulcinj, Bar and Budva were seized by the Venetians.'

correction.text: Zeta with Bar again ('Balsa seized Bar from the Venetians in 1412') but without Shkodër, Ulcinj and Budva

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Bar retaken in 1412; Ulcinj is never recovered on the page and Shkodër returns in 1418.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1418-1421: Zeta with Shkodër, 'conquered ... from the Venetians' in 1418

keyframe_review.note: 6,993 km2 matches Balsa III's Zeta (Montenegro 3,540 km2 plus the Albanian part around Shkodër), not the Serbian Despotate proper; it ends in 1421 when Zeta passes to Stefan Lazarević (the Serbian Despotate page: 'Area: not given', so no infobox comparison). Years only: 1415-1417 are covered by the 1412 keyframe, Ulcinj and Budva in the outline may be Venetian until 1421.

region.text: Zeta, the Lower Zeta around Lake Skadar, and the lands to the north and east held in 1375

ledger.note: 1371: the Balsic hold Zeta on their own. The family rose 'in the mid-14th century in the Lower Zeta region', was 'enthroned as rulers of the state under Tsar Urosh' in 1360 and 'created a regional principality sometime after 1360'; 'After the Battle of Marica in 1371, Emperor Urosh died in 1371 and no one succeeded him'. Founder Balsa I 'came to power in 1356'. The page gives no year for independence; 1371 is the year of Urosh's death. Second page, the Balšić noble family page: 'Following the Battle of Maritsa and the collapse of Serbian central state authority they were able to establish their own independent state' (infobox 'Serbian Empire (1355–71)', 'Lordship of Zeta (1355–1421)'). The Đurađ I page puts Prizren (taken from Marko) in 1371 and Peć a year later, so the Kosovo land of the 1375 outline comes with the founding.

region.text: the towns of Trebinje, Konavle and Dračevica (Herceg Novi)

ledger.note: c.1373: Đurađ I takes the coast beyond the Bay of Kotor from Nikola Altomanović. 'Đurađ gained the towns of Trebinje, Konavle and Dračevica (Herceg Novi) from Altomanović'; the page gives no single year. 1373 is Altomanović's defeat in the banate-of-bosnia dossier (Tvrtko I page, autumn 1373) and the first year of Fine's span on the Balšić page, which has the lands reaching 'north to the borders of Dubrovnik's territory' 'briefly between 1373 and 1377'. The counterpart string is the one banate-of-bosnia uses.

region.text: Dračevica, Konavle, Trebinje and the territories bordering Dubrovnik

ledger.note: 1377: Tvrtko I annexes the coast. 'Bosnian Ban Tvrtko I annexed Đurađ's territories bordering Dubrovnik in 1377'; the Balšić page has it as 'the coastal territories between Dubrovnik and the Bay of Kotor' at 'the end of the 1370s'. banate-of-bosnia records the same land as a gain in early 1377 (Tvrtko I page) with the free-text counterpart 'Djuradj I Balsic (Zeta)'; that row ends in October 1377 and kingdom-of-bosnia starts in 1385, so banate-of-bosnia is the slug here.

region.text: Prizren and other land in Kosovo

ledger.note: c.1378: Vuk Branković takes Prizren and the Kosovo land. 'The Balšić holdings declined at the end of the 1370s' ... 'while Vuk Branković took Prizren and other land in Kosovo.' The Đurađ I page (second page) places it after Đurađ I's death: 'Branković sent his forces into Metohija and seized Prizren, along with the rest of Đurađ's holdings in the region' (Đurađ I died 13 January 1378; a later study says 1379), so 1378 is the earliest year and the confidence is 2. Disagreement: the Đurađ II page lists 'Vuk Branković took Peć and Prizren' among the undated secessions after Savra (1385-86). district-of-brankovic has no dossier yet; moravian-serbia uses the free-text 'Vuk Branković' for the same lands in 1397.

By 1385: Balša II holds Durrës. 'By 1383 or 1385, Balša II had conquered Durrës, presumably from Karl Thopia', and in a charter to Ragusa he 'referred to himself as "Duke of Durrës"'. The page dates it only 'by 1383 or 1385', so 1385 is the later of the two (confidence 1). Mirrors albanian-principalities /ledger/3, which records the Durrës loss to this row in 1385.

18 September 1385: Karl Thopia recovers Durrës after Savra. 'Immediately after this battle Thopia recaptured Durrës, probably under the Ottoman suzerainty.' The Đurađ II page agrees: 'Before even consolidating rule, Karlo Thopia conquered Durrës and assigned it to his son George.' Mirrors albanian-principalities /ledger/5.

1386 (bridge): Pal Dukagjini takes Lezhë and the Drin area. 'Pal Dukagjini broke off allegiance to Đurađ, taking Lezhë and the Drin area.' The page gives no year; it narrates the loss among the secessions that follow Savra (18 September 1385). Lezhë stayed the Dukagjini centre until 1393 (Albanian principalities page), when, on the Đurađ II page, Đurađ tried to reclaim 'his old Lezhë' after the Dukagjinis had handed it to Venice. The Dukagjini lands belong to principality-of-dukagjini (no dossier yet); albanian-principalities has no mirror gain.

region.text: the Jonima family's own lands between Durrës and the Drin

ledger.note: 1386 (bridge): the Jonima family secedes with its lands. 'Finally the Jonima family seceded with their own lands between Durrës and the Drin, causing Đurađ to lose his very last possessions in Albania.' No year on the page; it follows the Dukagjini secession. The region is a radius because the page names only 'between Durrës and the Drin'. The Jonima are a local family without a dossier; albanian-principalities is the nearest Cliopatria row.

1386 (bridge): Onogošt goes to Venice. 'The area of Onogošt (Nikšić) seceded to the Venetians.' The page gives no year and puts the sentence just before 'In a short time, Đurađ's demesne had diminished into a small strip of land between Lake Skadar and the Adriatic Sea.' Mirror for republic-of-venice (eu-13).

After 1386 (bridge 1387): the castellan of Budva and his brother secede with the city. The page: 'his brother Andrija seceded the city after 1386' (Nikola Sakat is the castellan of Budva and Andrija his brother); Đurađ had the brothers imprisoned and blinded, undated. Budva is listed among Balsa III's lands in 1403 (Balsa III page), so it returns, undated.

March 1391: Đurađ II seizes Kotor. 'When Tvrtko died in the beginning of March 1391, the opportunity arose for Đurađ and he subsequently seized Kotor.' The page does not name the holder; Tvrtko's realm (kingdom-of-bosnia records Kotor as gained in 1385) is the reading. Disagreement with kingdom-of-bosnia /ledger/4, which records Kotor lost in 1391 to kingdom-of-hungary at confidence 1 (a bridge): this page has Đurađ II taking it, so that row should read serbian-despots. Kotor is lost again in 1392 (next entry) and is not among Balsa III's lands.

Late 1392 (bridge): while Đurađ II is a prisoner, Radič Crnojević takes the Kotor lands. 'Radič Crnojević captured his lands around Kotor and proclaimed himself Lord of Zeta and Budva.' The sentence follows the page's account of Đurađ's capture by the Ottoman bey in late 1392 and has no year of its own. The page later has Sandalj Hranić who 'conquered Budva and Kotor'; no page returns Kotor to the Balšići.

Early 1393: Ottoman squadrons occupy Scutari and Drivast. The Sultan 'sent an army to invade his lands in May 1392', Đurađ was captured in late 1392 and ransomed, and 'Ottoman squadrons occupied the locations in early 1393'; the page also says he handed Scutari and Drivast to the Ottomans in 1393.

region.text: Scutari, Lake Skadar with its islands, and Sveti Srđ

ledger.note: April 1396: Đurađ II hands Scutari to Venice. 'In April 1396 a contract was signed'; he 'handed over Scutari, the Skadar Lake with all its islands and Sveti Srđ to Venetian administration' (Drivast with it); in May Venice moved against him. Venice's Stato da Mar record has Scutari Venetian 1396-1479.
1396: the Ottomans no longer hold Scutari. The page does not say when the Ottoman occupation ended; Đurađ II could cede the town to Venice only after it, so April 1396 is the latest bridge.
1405: Venice seizes Ulcinj, Bar and Budva. 'In 1405, Ulcinj, Bar and Budva were seized by the Venetians.'
1412: Balsa III retakes Bar. 'Balša seized Bar from the Venetians in 1412.'

1418: Balsa III retakes Shkodër. 'In 1418, he conquered Shkodër from the Venetians.' An attempt on Budva in 1419 failed. The page continues: 'but lost Budva and Luštica with its salt works' (no holder named; Budva is listed as seized by Venice in 1405 on the same page, with no recovery).

region.text: the towns of Bar and Ulcinj

ledger.note: 1421, after Balša III's death on 28 April: 'Later that year, the Republic of Venice took advantage of Balša's death and seized the towns of Bar and Ulcinj,' and 'some of his other territories were seized by the Ottomans and Bosnians' (the page names Balša III as the one who died in 1421). Only Bar is in the region: the Balša III page has Ulcinj already seized by Venice in 1405 and never recovered. The Ottoman and Bosnian seizures are undated and unnamed; see notes.

1421: Zeta passes to Stefan Lazarević. 'In 1421, before his death and under the influence of his mother, he passed the rule of Zeta to his uncle, Despot Stefan Lazarević'; Balsa III died on 28 April 1421, 'the Balšić family was succeeded by the House of Lazarević' (Principality of Zeta page).

wars.name: Battle of Savra

zones.text: Durres and the plain near Berat

wars.outcome: Balsa II, defeated and killed on 18 September 1385 'near Berat in battle against the Turks'; Đurađ II succeeds; Thopia recovers Durres.

wars.name: Ottoman invasion of Zeta (Đurađ II)
wars.outcome: The Sultan's army invaded in May 1392; Đurađ II was captured in late 1392 and ransomed; Ottoman squadrons occupied the places in early 1393.
wars.note: He is described as an Ottoman vassal until about 1395 and then took Venetian citizenship in May 1395.

wars.name: Balsa III's war with Venice (First Scutari War)
wars.outcome: Venice seized Ulcinj, Bar and Budva in 1405; Balsa III retook Bar in 1412 and Shkodër in 1418 and failed at Budva in 1419.
wars.note: The page calls it 'a 10-year war' without a span and does not name the Second Scutari War (1419-1423).

certainty.note: No treaty line is given on any page opened; Zeta's borders follow the towns held (Scutari, Ulcinj, Bar, Kotor) and the Venetian frontier moves with them.

sources.note: Why the row is not the Despotate: established 22 February 1402, predecessors include 'Zeta under the Balsici', Zeta incorporated in 1421; no area given.

sources.note: Thin page: Balsa I 1356, 1360 enthronement, regional principality after 1360, Marica 1371, Lazarevic succession 1421.

Re-read for the repair: the holders of the lands lost after Savra (Dukagjini, Jonima, Venice, the Sakat brothers, Branković), Kotor and the Crnojević.

sources.note: 18 September 1385, the death of Balsa II near Berat. Re-read: Durrës held 'by 1383 or 1385', recaptured by Thopia immediately after the battle.

sources.title: Albanian principalities
sources.note: Used for the Dukagjini centre at Lezhë until 1393 (note to the 1388 loss).

sources.title: Balšić noble family
sources.note: Opened on the reviewer's pointer (the earlier try used a title that does not exist): infobox 'Lordship of Zeta (1355–1421)', no area; Shkodër the centre 1355-1396; decline 'at the end of the 1370s' (Branković and Prizren, Tvrtko and the coast); Venice and Bar and Ulcinj 'later that year' after Balša III's death in 1421.

notes: REPAIRED 2026-11-01 after review (verdict fail). WHAT THE ROW IS: Cliopatria's 'Serbian Despots' (1375-1421, Wikipedia field 'Serbian Despotate', Q878319) is not the Serbian Despotate (founded 22 February 1402, Belgrade and Smederevo, ended 20 June 1459: that is the moravian-serbia dossier). Its 6,993 km2 shape of 1415-1421 and its end in 1421 are Zeta under Balsa III, which the Despotate absorbed in 1421; the 1375-1394 shape (29,468 km2) is Zeta, the Albanian coast and Kosovo under the Balšići. Slug kept; identity.name 'Zeta (Balšić lordship)'; identity.wikipedia is now 'Balšić noble family' (infobox 'Lordship of Zeta (1355–1421)') and wikidata null (Q878319 is the Despotate's). PAGES: Serbian Despotate, Principality of Zeta (thin), Balša III, Đurađ II Balšić, Battle of Savra, Albanian principalities, and, in the repair, Balšić noble family and Đurađ I Balšić. The page budget (5) is exceeded by two pages, both on the reviewer's pointer or needed for the dates it asked for. CHANGES: (1) the invented quote of the old 1388 loss is gone: the page names each holder, so the loss is split into Lezhë and the Drin (Pal Dukagjini, albanian-principalities), the Jonima lands (albanian-principalities), Onogošt (republic-of-venice) and Budva (the Sakat brothers, after 1386), all dated by the page's order only (1386, 1387; confidence 1). (2) The fall from 29,468 km2 is now explained: the coast from Trebinje to Dračevica is gained about 1373 and annexed by Tvrtko in 1377 (Đurađ I page, 'in 1377'), Prizren and Kosovo go to Vuk Branković about 1378, and the keyframes 1371, 1373, 1375 (1377 only), 1378 and 1386 follow them. (3) Durrës 1385 mirrors albanian-principalities. (4) Kotor: counterpart kept as kingdom-of-bosnia; a loss to Radič Crnojević is added for 1392; the 1391 hand-over is contradicted by kingdom-of-bosnia /ledger/4 (Hungary). (5) Rulers Đurađ I and Balša II from the Đurađ I page; capital 1 now rests on the Balšić page. (6) 1421: Venice seizes Bar (Balšić page). WHERE I DISAGREE OR AM UNSURE: the reviewer put the Kosovo and coast losses 'c.1378-1379'; the Đurađ I page dates the coast to 1377, so the coast is in 1377 and Kosovo in 1378. The Đurađ II page lists Branković's taking of Peć and Prizren after Savra; the two Balšić pages put Prizren in the late 1370s, and Peć is named only on the Đurađ II page (Đurađ I took it in 1372 from Marko, per the Đurađ I page). Cliopatria's 1375 shape holds Kosovo, the Albanian coast and the Zeta interior but no cell of Herceg Novi or Trebinje; the 1373 keyframe adds them. The ~8,000 km2 of Zeta interior that disappears between the 1378 and 1386 keyframes has no holder on any page (Radič Crnojević is the only name). Pages silent on: Balsa III's seat 1405-1417 (Balša III page re-read: no seat named, he went to Belgrade in 1419), the Ottoman and Bosnian seizures after 1421 (Balšić page, undated), who held Kotor before March 1391, the dates of Balša I, Stracimir and the Balšić gains before 1371. Not in the ledger because they belong to the suzerain: the Ottoman vassalage of Đurađ II and Balsa III, the Serbian influence from 1405 (moravian-serbia carries vassal_start 1405 and vassal_end 1421 with counterpart serbian-despots). Mirrors still to be made by others: republic-of-venice (Scutari 1396 should read serbian-despots; Onogošt 1386; Ulcinj, Bar, Budva 1405; Bar 1412; Shkodër 1418; Bar 1421), albanian-principalities (Lezhë/Drin 1386 and the Jonima lands 1386 gain; Durrës loss/gain 1385 is already there), kingdom-of-bosnia (Kotor 1391 to this row), banate-of-bosnia (its free-text counterpart 'Djuradj I Balsic (Zeta)' for the 1377 gain could read serbian-despots). Gazetteer: all names used resolve (Lake Skadar, Shkodër, Ulcinj, Bar, Budva, Kotor, Lezhë, Niksic, Herceg Novi, Trebinje, Kosovo, Durrës); Konavle is a coordinate radius.
